text:
alex: heads up — acme-inc seeing intermittent 429s on dedicated/reserved-a since ~09:15 UTC. They report steady baseline traffic but errors spike every ~5–10m for ~20–40s. Pool metrics look healthy (no OOMs). Suspect per-tenant quota translation + noisy-neighbor spillback. attaching brief logs/snips.

evan: can you paste the exact 429 response and a sample request-id? also confirm tenant id.

alex: tenant id: acme-prod-42. example response from earlier today: 
```bash
curl -i https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H \"Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>\" -d '{"model":"rwd-4x","input":"hi"}'
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-request-id: req-0a1b2c3d
x-quota-reason: tenant_rate_limit
{"error":"quota_exceeded","detail":"rate units exceeded"}
```

ops-bot: alert: reserved-a pool status — GPU mem 78%, GPU util 42%, autoscaler stable, no node evictions. No infra-level failures.

sam: quick read — quota subsystem returned tenant_rate_limit at the 429s. Two likely vectors: (1) a recent quota translation multiplier change (plan units -> rate units) or (2) a pacing window mis-apply causing short bursts to count double. We rolled a small mapping change yesterday.

maya: billing/quotas shows acme-prod-42 got a manual cap yesterday via support ticket #8219: cap = 2000 rate-units/min. If the translation multiplier increased from 1x -> 3x, effective cap would drop to ~666 requests/min which matches their observed spike threshold.

evan: repro plan: in staging, run steady 100rps from acme-prod-42 and then ramp a co-tenanted noisy tenant in same reserved-A pool to 120rps for 60s. If quota translation is wrong we'll see spillback 429s on the steady tenant. I can schedule a window. Do we want a prod window too?

alex: staging first please. can you also capture traces for x-request-ids that show the quota code path?

evan: yup. sample load snippet I'm using: 
```python
import requests
for i in range(60000):
    r = requests.post("https://staging-api.redwood.example/v1/generate", json={\"model\":\"rwd-4x\", \"input\":\"spam\"}, headers={\"Authorization\":\"Bearer STAGING_KEY\", \"X-Tenant\":\"acme-prod-42\"})
    if r.status_code == 429:
        print("429 @", i, r.headers.get('x-request-id'))
```

sam: mitigation options while we triage: (A) temporary per-tenant quota override (bump cap to 6k units/min), (B) enable soft-fallback to a lower-cost compatible model variant for that tenant to avoid unit burn, (C) rollback the translation change if staging reproduces. Option A is fastest.

maya: I can apply an override now if eng-oncall approves. That would stop customer-facing 429s immediately.

evan: I approve option A for a short window (30–60m) while we run staging repro and collect traces. I'll also run a canary revert of the translation mapping in staging.

alex: thanks — i'll tell the customer we're doing a temporary override and we'll follow up with root-cause. saving request-ids + traces to the support ticket. :thumbsup: 

support-bot: incident IR-4321 created and linked to support ticket #8219. assigned: eng-oncall, priority: P2.

alex: next steps: (1) maya pushes override now, (2) evan runs staging repro and posts traces, (3) sam prepares rollback plan for mapping change. i'll update acme thread with ETA.
